title: Timeouts and retries
summary: Timeouts bound waiting, while controlled retries recover from some transient failures.
overview: A timed-out request may already have changed remote state. Retries therefore need safe operation semantics, bounded attempts, and backoff with jitter to avoid synchronized load.
why: Aggressive retries can amplify an outage rather than recover from it.
example: A checkout client retries a transient connection failure using the same idempotency key, with randomized delay and an overall deadline.
judgment: Choose retryable failures, latency budgets, and which layer owns retries.
next: How many downstream attempts can one user request generate across all retrying layers?
